DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wvm.dilg.com.ph .10 SEP 2019 OiLG OPINION NO. HON. CHONA R. DE LEON Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Daanbantayan Province of Cebu Dear SB Member De Leon: This has reference to your letter dated 3 October 2018, requesting the Department's appropriate action on Mayor Vicente Loot's unauthorized absences in the Municipal Office since July 2018 which is contrary to Section 444(c)1 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code (LGC). Per your letter, his physical absence without filing leave of absence hampered community services because some constituents need his personal advice and counseling. Further, functioning as an INVISIBLE MAYOR is INAPPROPRIATE because a Mayor's Office is a public trust and the Mayor must be visible and available, his office must be in public place and mandated by law in which he can receive and attend the constituents call or matters dispensable by and related to the functions of his office. Hence, you are now seeking this Department's appropriate action. At the outset, Section 444(c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 requires the incumbent municipal mayor to hold office at the municipal hall. To our view, this is imperative in order for the said official to effectively, efficiently and economically perform his duties and responsibilities to his constituents, as mandated under the law. More importantly, the Mayor's presence in his area of jurisdiction is indispensable, in order for the latter to be aware and be responsive to any unexpected events and situations affecting the general welfare of his municipality. On the same token, considering that the basic function of the appointive officials you mentioned is to assist and coordinate with the mayor in ensuring the proper management of the political and administrative affairs of the municipality, it is but imperative also, that they should likewise hold their office in the municipal ha112. SECTION 444. The Chief Executive; Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. xxx (c) During his incumbency, the municipal mayor shall hold office in the municipal hall. 2 DILG OPINION NO. 033-05, dated 18 May 2005

Thus, this Department agrees with you that Mayor Loot's absences in the Municipal Office since July 2018 is contrary to Section 444(c) of the LGC. Pursuant to Section 603 of the LGC, unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive days is already a ground for a disciplinary action against local elective officials. In the herein case, the absences incurred by Mayor Loot is already more than fifteen (15) consecutive days. Hence, an appropriate administrative complaint against Mayor Loot may already be filed in accordance with Section 614 of the LGC. Accordingly, may we advise you that the corresponding administrative complaint against Mayor Loot may already be filed with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cebu by any concerned citizen, including you. CC: We hope we have assisted you on the matter accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secret MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Dir. Leocadio T. Trovela Regional Director DILG- egion VII Ls/9 3SECTlON 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. - An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: (a) Disloyalty to the Republic of the Philippines; (b) Culpable violation of the Constitution; (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; (e) Abuse of authority; (f) Unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive working days, except in the case of members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, Sangguniang bayan, and Sangguniang Barangay; (g) Application for, or acquisition of, foreign citizenship or residence or the status of an immigrant of another country; and (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. 4 SECTION 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective Official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A complaint against any elective Barangay official shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory.
